one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window. (1) Q3 2026 earnings, estimated for Monday Oct 26 after the close. The date is still not company-confirmed: no Q3 webcast notice had been issued as of Oct 1, while the Q2 notice came Jul 6, three weeks before that print [38]. A notice is due in the next few days. Q3 guidance is $1.595-1.625B revenue and $2.01-2.07 non-GAAP EPS, with an $8.1B backlog. The FY26 EPS guide has already recovered the Hexagon dilution (Q1 cut to $7.85-7.95, Q2 raised back to $8.05-8.15) [33][1], so a further modest raise is the base case. The reaction base rate is not bullish, though: 41% of 17 prints had a positive first day, with a median up move of +7% and a median down move of -2% (Trefis) [32]. Synopsys's read-through is the same lesson: +13.4% the day after its August beat, then -21% by Sep 15 in the rate and software sell-off (supervisor's Twelve Data check). Beats are rewarded on the day but give no directional edge over a month. (2) The FOMC on Oct 28: Polymarket 74% hold / 26% +25bp, about $21.4M volume [15]. The 10-year is at 5.29% [14]. Short-horizon setup: the stock is up 28% in 12 sessions from $273.96, a rally driven partly by the Synopsys investor-day sympathy move and a Morgan Stanley PT raise to $400 [39]. In CDNS's own history, the month after a gain of more than 12% has a median return of about 0% (n=20). So I centre at about $351.5 with a monthly sigma of about 12.5%. That is 41%/3.5 = 11.7%, plus an earnings and FOMC bump; recent weekly vol of 41% annualised [36] confirms the 41% input. The distribution is roughly lognormal and near symmetric.

fair_value.method: Blended 12-month-forward value of $352 (round 1: $348). Weights: 50% P/E (blended NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of $10.65 x 34x = $362), 35% FCF yield (NTM FCF/share of about $8.70 at a 2.4% yield = $362) and 15% DCF (WACC 10% from a 5.29% 10-year + 1.14 beta x 4.23% ERP, giving $293 forward). A reverse DCF shows that spot already implies about 25% 5-year FCF growth at a 10% WACC.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Blended NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of $10.65 (0.25 x FY27 consensus $9.56 + 0.75 x FY28 estimate ~$11.0) x 34x

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 guide path: $8.05-8.15 in Feb (ex-Hexagon) [34], cut to $7.85-7.95 in Q1 to absorb Hexagon dilution [33], raised back to $8.05-8.15 in Q2 [1]. Organic beats recovered the Hexagon dilution within the year, which supports the FY27 consensus rather than a haircut.

StockAnalysis consensus across 26 analysts, confirmed by the supervisor as the broad consensus (Zacks $9.43-9.54 a touch lower). I do not haircut it, given the FY26 guide path recovered Hexagon dilution [1][33][34].

FY27 consensus of $9.56 grown about 15%. That matches FY26's 14% EPS growth and Synopsys's new mid-teens EPS CAGR framework to FY2030 for the same end-market. Cadence management also flagged possible 2027 margin improvement after the Hexagon integration.
0.25 x 9.56 + 0.75 x 11.0. This corrects round 1, which used the FY28 figure of $11.0 itself as the blended NTM.

CDNS is at 38.5x forward today (StockAnalysis). The 10-year TTM P/E range is about 16-101x (GuruFocus). SNPS is at about 25x FY27 EPS ($475.70 / $19.08 guide) after its investor day re-rating. The 10-year Treasury at 5.29% (H.15) is about 1 point higher than I assumed in round 1, which argues for more compression than the 36x I used then. I keep a premium to SNPS for hardware and IP momentum.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF/share at Oct-2027 of about $8.70 / 2.4% yield

inputs_detail.value: ~276.5M (FY26 diluted guide 275-277M at Q1, 275.5-277.5M at Q2)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 FCF of about $1.84B (OCF $2.0B less about $0.16B capex) / 276.5M shares = $6.65. Grown about 17% gives FY27 $7.80 and FY28 about $9.0, blended 0.25/0.75 to $8.70. The growth is cross-checked against Synopsys's guide of mid-20s FCF CAGR to FY30, which I deliberately fade. This is an equity-level yield (FCF per share / price), so no net-debt adjustment applies. Management returns about 50% of FCF via buybacks [33], so the share count drifts only slightly lower and is left at 276.5M.
The current P/FCF of 56x is a 1.8% yield. I de-rate it to about 42x, consistent with the P/E method and a 5.29% risk-free rate.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCF0 $1.84B; growth 18% for years 1-5 and 12% for years 6-10; terminal growth 4%; WACC 10% (5.29% 10-year + beta 1.14 x 4.23% ERP = 10.1%); net debt $1.12B; 276.5M shares. Value today $266, rolled forward to $293. Sensitivity: WACC 9.5% gives $294 today / $322 forward, 9% gives $357 forward. Reverse DCF: $350.73 today needs about 25% FCF growth for 5 years (then 12%) at a 10% WACC, or about 22% at 9.5%.

inputs_detail.derivation: 2026 revenue growth guide of 19%, record $8.1B backlog, and management's possible 2027 margin improvement. Synopsys guides mid-20s FCF CAGR to FY30. I set this slightly below revenue growth plus margin.

The risk-free rate is the 10-year at 5.29% (H.15, Sep 30, 2026) [14]. I use the 10-year rather than the 3-month bill (4.03%) because the cash flows are long-dated. Beta is 1.14 [9]. The ERP is 4.23%, Damodaran's January-2026 implied US ERP [37]. 5.29% + 1.14 x 4.23% = 10.1%, rounded to 10%. Each 50bp of WACC moves the forward value by about $30/share.
EDA is a secular grower: Synopsys targets 13%+ EDA CAGR to FY2030. I fade that toward nominal GDP plus.

inputs_detail.value: ~25% FCF CAGR for years 1-5 at 10% WACC (~22% at 9.5%)
inputs_detail.derivation: Solved for the years 1-5 growth that sets the DCF equal to $350.73, holding years 6-10 at 12% and terminal growth at 4%. That growth sits at Synopsys's own mid-20s FCF CAGR target to FY30 [11], which is a bull-case assumption for Cadence. So spot already prices a lot of execution, and the DCF stays at low weight as a check on the multiple methods.

bear.story: The multiple compresses to about 23-24x NTM EPS of about $10.4, i.e. Synopsys parity. Possible triggers: rates keep climbing (10-year at 5.29%, 26% odds of an October hike); the AI-disruption narrative returns (Kimi K3, -9.5% on Jul 17, 2026; funded AI-native EDA start-ups); or China (15% of Q2 revenue, up from 13% in Q1) loses access when the BIS Affiliates Rule suspension ends on Jan 10, 2027, just before the Feb FY27 guide [35][33]. A conservative initial FY27 guide (FY26 also started low, at $8.05-8.15 ex-Hexagon [34]) or a 2027 recession (Kalshi about 20%) would add to this. Ends near or below the 2026 lows ($262.75).

base.story: 15-19% revenue growth, with FY27 EPS near the $9.56 consensus (the FY26 guide path shows organic beats absorbing Hexagon dilution) and blended NTM EPS of about $10.65 at about 34x. EPS growth is partly eaten by further de-rating under high yields, as over the past year (price -0.2% while EPS grew about 14%).

bull.story: Agentic AI (ChipStack, ViraStack; consumption revenue excluded from guidance) and record hardware demand lift FY27-28 estimates to about $11.4 NTM, and the 2025-26 peak multiple of about 42x returns. Synopsys's FY27 +15% guide and mid-teens long-term model support the sector, and yields ease from multi-decade highs. FCF growth reaches the roughly 25% the reverse DCF says spot already needs. Breaks the $416.69 52-week high.

thesis_break_reason: $245 is about 7% below the 52-week low of $262.75 and about 23x NTM EPS at the horizon, below Synopsys's roughly 25x FY27. Sentiment and yields alone took CDNS to $273.96 on Sep 15, 2026 with no company news, and the stock also held about $274-330 through the July AI-disruption scare. So levels in the $260s-270s are proven noise. Trading at $245 would most likely require fundamental damage: an FY27 guide well below about 13% growth, backlog falling from $8.1B, visible agent-driven seat or price compression, or China access lost when the Affiliates Rule suspension ends on Jan 10, 2027 [35]. The 2025 trough of about $221 needed the April 2025 tariff shock plus the BIS EDA ban.

reasoning: Base rates. CDNS month-end closes 2006-2026 [3]: forward 12-month log returns have a median of +20% and SD 0.36 (last 10 years: median +27%, SD 0.20). As the supervisor stressed, that drift is inflated by the 2010s re-rating. The current regime is about +13% a year over 3 years, flat over the past year while EPS grew about 14%, so I give the historical drift almost no weight. I centre the 12-month median at $358, close to my $352 fair value plus a little EPS-driven drift. On volatility, I took the supervisor's point that my monthly-close vol (29-31%) understated risk, and rechecked it on weekly closes [36]: 41.3% annualised over the last 52 weeks, 39.3% over 104 weeks and 38.4% since Aug 2021; non-overlapping 4-week returns give 34%. The true horizon vol is therefore nearer 37-40% than 30%. I use a lognormal core with sigma 0.37 plus a 15% fat-tail component at sigma 0.55. That puts slightly more mass below $281 than round 1 and leaves the upper strikes about unchanged. Valuation: the supervisor confirmed NTM EPS of about $10.65 and the rates inputs, so the P/E leg stays $362. The FY26 guide path (Feb $8.05-8.15 ex-Hexagon, Q1 $7.85-7.95, Q2 back to $8.05-8.15 [34][33][1]) is a mild positive for the FY27 consensus. I now state the ERP explicitly: 4.23% (Damodaran, Jan 2026 [37]) gives a 10.1% WACC. DCF sensitivity is about $30/share per 50bp, and a reverse DCF shows $351 needs about 25% FCF growth, so I cut the DCF weight to 15% and moved that weight to the FCF-yield leg: fair value $352. Events and policy: Polymarket Oct FOMC 74/26 ($21.4M); Kalshi 2027 recession about 20%; Taiwan invasion by end-2027 13% ($3.3M). The BIS Affiliates Rule suspension now runs to Jan 10, 2027 [35]. It is a separate rule from the May-2025 EDA licence regime that was lifted in July 2025, so China risk is deferred, not removed. I also corrected China's share of revenue to 13% (Q1) and 15% (Q2). The Q3 date remains unconfirmed [38]. Scenarios of $250/$365/$480 at 25/50/25 give an EV of about $365, a little above the $358 median because of right skew. The sell-side average target of $405 is evidence, not an anchor. Research this round was limited to 6 queries and fetches.
